Honeypot is a term for a scam token or contract in which buyers can purchase the asset but are blocked from selling it. Honeypot schemes trap investors' funds because the sell function is restricted for everyone except the scammer. Honeypot tokens typically lure victims with the appearance of a legitimate, tradable asset.

Front-running is the practice of executing a transaction ahead of another user's pending transaction after observing it in the mempool. Front-running usually relies on paying a higher transaction fee so that the transaction is included first. Front-running profits from the price movement that the victim's transaction is expected to cause.

Air Gap refers to a device, such as a wallet or signing machine, that is kept isolated from internet connections. Air Gap setups are used to protect private keys from online attacks. Air Gap storage keeps signing operations separated from networked systems.

Apeing is the act of buying a token quickly and without research, usually driven by hype or social media momentum. Apeing involves impulsive investment decisions rather than careful due diligence. Apeing exposes buyers to high losses when the hyped asset collapses.

Bank Run describes a situation in which many depositors or holders withdraw their funds at the same time out of fear of insolvency. Bank Run events can force a protocol or platform to fail because its liquid reserves are insufficient to meet all withdrawals. Bank Run dynamics are self-fulfilling, since panic about withdrawals drives more withdrawals.
